heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, video creation, and multimodal visual workflows.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed brand-orange hero with a premium mesh-gradient overlay and floating glass chips, avoiding a split layout. Place a large layered product proof cluster on the right/upper plane of the hero canvas: one prompt-to-image card, one cinematic video frame strip, one waveform/lip-sync chip, and a thin logo marquee for trust. Keep the H1 extremely prominent on the left with generous whitespace, but not centered. Use dark near-black micro-panels and soft glass surfaces within the orange field for contrast. The CTA should be a solid Techjockey orange-accent button with rounded shape and strong hover lift. This hero should feel editorial, enterprise-grade, and cinematic rather than generic AI-futuristic.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a full-bleed orange, content-first overlay with cinematic product chips
Trust is immediate and logo-led, but shifts into a dark proof band to change pace
Product sections alternate between bright editorial and dark immersive panels
Testimonials are compact and credibility-focused to avoid another dense feature block
Pricing is presented as a highlighted card pair rather than a generic table
Final CTA is isolated in a centered lead form for a clean conversion finish
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create premium AI images and videos with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance. Explore the workflow, see logo-backed proof, compare capabilities, and get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: orange gradient base with floating orbs, subtle model-output collage, and soft dark overlay for contrast
sections.designNote: Make this content-first and dynamic above the fold. Lead with the headline that clearly says what the product is, the subheadline that names the audience, and a single full-width mobile CTA labeled Get started. Add compact trust bullets beneath the copy, but keep the visual energy high with abstract AI output frames and floating chips.

Use 3-6 recognisable logos in a fast, premium marquee right after the hero. This should feel like immediate enterprise validation. If logo set is thin, swap to a metric strip, but default to logos-first because the traffic is warm and trust needs to land early.

Use two alternating product blocks rather than a generic SaaS feature grid. The first block should be a bright editorial section focused on Seedream 4.5 with a visual preview and accordion-style feature depth because there are 5+ features. The second block should flip to a dark immersive section for Seedance 1.5 Pro, with cinematic motion cues, audio-wave visuals, and the same single CTA label Get started.

Use this as a concise credibility break, not a long persuasion block. Present a small icon-card grid with enterprise-readiness, guided evaluation, implementation support, and commercial credibility. Keep it visually lighter in density but dark in tone to create contrast after the product sections.

Show two premium pricing cards with the image model and the video model separated clearly. Avoid a table. The visual emphasis should feel like a selection moment, with the video plan slightly more prominent if you want stronger commercial hierarchy. Every CTA remains Get started and should be solid accent orange.

Because there are 5 testimonials, use a carousel or slider rather than a static grid. Keep it compact and role-led: Creative Director, Video Producer, Art Director, Marketing Manager, Creative Lead. This is proof, not a story section, so the cards should be crisp and easy to scan.

End with a focused conversion block, visually isolated from prior sections. Make it feel like the final action step after proof and pricing. Keep the form minimal, use a strong headline, and make the only button Get started in solid orange at full opacity.

If media/logos are available, use this as a lightweight footer-adjacent credibility strip. If not, omit or convert it into a restrained brand-recognition band. Do not make it compete with the CTA section.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium, creative, and commercially credible — like an AI studio built for enterprise marketing teams, with strong logo-led trust, warm brand energy, and polished motion that feels intelligent rather than noisy.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use premium AI-generated abstract product visuals rather than literal stock imagery: layered model output previews, cinematic frame strips, mock prompt-to-result panels, audio waveforms, and floating output chips. Keep logos as the dominant trust element in a marquee band near the hero and again near pricing. Use SVG for logos and icons, PNG for product UI shells, and JPEG only for the hero’s large atmospheric visual area if needed.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and detail-heavy, so it needs a smaller hero size to stay elegant and avoid awkward line breaks while still feeling premium.

colours.colourReason: Techjockey brand colors define the palette: orange must lead the hero and CTA, with white, near-black, and soft grey used for contrast and structure. This creates a distinctive identity without drifting into an unapproved generic AI purple palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with a strong headline, short supporting copy, and a primary action; visually treated as a high-contrast banner rather than a media-led showcase. Typography-forward layout with compact trust bullets beneath the value proposition.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column story flow with a top hero, followed by content blocks that read like stacked feature sections. Minimal branching; emphasis is on linear progression from overview to detailed capabilities to conversion form.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple content cards/panels with light borders or subtle elevation implied by the form module; utility-first and functional rather than decorative. No evidence of glassmorphism, hover-heavy presentation, or dense card grids.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is singular and prominently placed in the hero; secondary CTA presence is minimal or absent. Downstream sections use a conversion-oriented request/demo action rather than multiple competing actions.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing section present in the reference layout.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided markup; likely minimal or standard utility footer outside the captured frame.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Text-first layout with limited visible media in the captured hero. The design favors brand/logo presence and content blocks over product imagery, large illustrations, or video embeds.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with headline, supporting paragraph, and a list of capability points. Best interpreted as progressive disclosure: overview first, then detail-level benefits in bullet-like subpoints.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form card placed below the hero, visually separated as a conversion zone. Uses hidden tracking fields and a compact field stack, suggesting friction-reducing, form-driven inquiry rather than checkout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-oriented page behavior with no clear evidence of motion systems beyond possible standard form validation and basic responsive adjustments.
designNotes: Prioritize clarity, trust, and lead generation over visual theatrics.
Use a strong hero with concise benefit bullets and a single dominant CTA.
Follow with vertically stacked feature sections that explain capabilities in digestible chunks.
Keep surfaces mostly clean and editorial, with whitespace separating content and form zones.
Avoid carousel-heavy or tabbed interaction patterns unless additional content volume requires compression.
Use a dedicated form panel as the primary conversion module rather than embedding CTAs throughout the page.

blueprint.additionalInstructions: PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

mustHaveMoments: Logo-first trust strip near the hero to establish credibility immediately
Clear product split in the hero between Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Primary CTA above the fold with a demo or quote-oriented conversion path
Dedicated feature sections for image generation and video generation with concise capability summaries
Pricing or quote framing placed after capability proof to support evaluation
Testimonial section with role-based quotes from creative and marketing decision-makers
Footer with standard utility links and contact reassurance
avoidPatterns: Media-heavy hero layouts that dilute the message
Badge-only trust without visible brand/logo proof
Overly decorative or experimental visual styling
Dense comparison grids that make the page feel like a product catalog
Long-form technical explanation before establishing value
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best positioned as a lead-generation landing page for solution-aware buyers who already understand generative AI but need confidence in product capability and vendor credibility. Because the instruction says visitors trust logos most, trust should be built primarily through prominent brand/logo placement rather than badge stacks or stats. The content is strongly product-led, with two distinct but related AI offerings, so the hero should quickly clarify both products and the outcomes they deliver. A split hero supports fast comprehension while keeping the page linear and conversion-focused. CTA pressure should be moderate: strong enough to drive demo/quote intent, but not aggressive enough to overwhelm enterprise evaluators. Balanced section density fits the long-content requirement and the technical nature of the offer, while still keeping the experience readable and premium.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
